_comment: stream-json kinds seen in a real run that still reach ProviderEvent.Unknown — seen, and deliberately not modelled. Read by src/smoke.ts, which used to restate the list; pnpm smoke fails when a kind outside it turns up. A kind is a key and its reason is the value, so an entry without one cannot be written.
_empty: EMPTY IS THE GOAL. It stops being true the moment a known kind is left out of the vocabulary for convenience, which is what system/thinking_tokens, user, rate_limit_event and system/background_tasks_changed each did until they were named. Add an entry only with a reason for why the concept cannot be modelled; prefer modelling it. None of the claude kinds below has ever been seen by pnpm smoke, whose prompt neither delegates, runs a slow tool nor touches git: the first four were found by hand in the corpus and in test/fixtures/claude/background-work.captured.jsonl and slow-command.captured.jsonl, the rest in another project's transcripts. Recognised-and-silent is a third answer and not this one — an inline shell task's task_started is read and emits nothing, which is why it is not here.

claude.system/task_progress: everything it carries is already stored. It reports a running subagent's last tool name and its token and duration counters; the subagent's own tool rows are stored entries saying the same thing, and the client's live preview is the most recent of them. Modelling it would roughly double the rows a subagent writes.
claude.system/task_updated: it carries no tool_use_id — only a task_id — so joining it to the call it belongs to needs memory of the task_started before it, and claudeNormalizeLine is stateless by design. It arrives immediately BEFORE task_notification, which names the same task, carries strictly more, and is modelled. Its patch.status also spells a stop differently — killed where the notification says stopped — so modelling both would put two vocabularies for one fact on the wire.
claude.tool_progress: a heartbeat, emitted every 30s for calls the CLI registers a task for. Its elapsed_time_seconds is the only thing on it we do not already have, and the recorded `at` on every transcript entry is a better source: it is exact, it exists for every call rather than for the registered ones, and folding a heartbeat into a row would mean mutating a line of an append-only file. Its repl_call and subagent_retry variants carry an inner tool and a subagent's own retry counters — neither has a consumer while a delegation is drawn one level deep.
claude.system/commands_changed: the full slash-command list after a mid-session change, pushed for a client that caches one. Nothing here caches commands and no transcript row could be made of it.
claude.system/code_change_published: the CLI noticing that the turn opened or updated a pull request — provider, url, repository, action. The call that did it is already a row, and the pull request a trak lands is the engine's own record, read from the forge rather than from what an agent said it published. A second, unjoined copy of that fact in the transcript has nothing to add to either.
claude.system/vcs_state_changed: the CLI noticing a commit, push, merge or rebase in the session's checkout — a kind and sometimes a branch. The git command that caused it is already a row, and what a worktree's branch holds is read from git by the engine, which is the source this would be a lagging copy of.
claude.system/informational: a notice-level line of the CLI's own prose (`content`, `level: notice`) written for its interactive interface. It is not something the agent did or said, and its wording is the CLI's to change between releases, so nothing could be keyed on it.

codex.item.completed/error: a warning the turn survives — `Model metadata for x not found`, before the API then refuses the model. Nothing in the vocabulary is a warning: it is not an ApiError, which fails the turn, and not text the agent wrote. When the turn does fail, the ApiError that ends it says so; a warning kind would be one entry for a line that, on its own, changes nothing a reader does.
